themes_detail.label: Building Code Violations Surge
themes_detail.summary: Building/Use complaints spiked to 27 THIS WEEK—a 360% jump from the 5.9-complaint weekly average over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 7.1)—suggesting a sudden wave of code violations or enforcement activity in Sunset Park that warrants immediate investigation.
evidence: 27 Building/Use complaints THIS WEEK vs. 5.9 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
360% spike with z-score of 7.1 (statistically severe anomaly)
622 total DOB building permits filed in last 90 days (432 alterations), suggesting active construction/renovation activity
reporting_angles: Coordinate with DOB to identify what types of violations are driving the spike and which buildings are affected
Interview residents in blocks with multiple complaints to understand safety concerns (electrical, structural, occupancy violations)

themes_detail.label: Noise Crisis Spreading
themes_detail.summary: Overall noise complaints jumped 160% THIS WEEK to 25 complaints vs. 9.6 weekly average (z-score: 4.93), with vehicle noise up 211% (14 vs. 4.5) and park noise up 700% (4 vs. 0.5), indicating a multi-source noise problem accelerating across the district this week.
evidence: 25 total noise complaints THIS WEEK vs. 9.6 weekly average (160% increase, z-score: 4.93)
Vehicle noise: 14 complaints THIS WEEK vs. 4.5 weekly average (211% spike, z-score: 4.75)
Park noise: 4 complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.5 weekly average (700% spike, z-score: 4.95)
reporting_angles: Interview residents near parks and major traffic corridors about timing, sources, and impact on sleep/quality of life
Investigate whether specific events, construction, or enforcement gaps are driving the park and vehicle noise spikes

themes_detail.label: Food Safety Contamination Pattern
themes_detail.summary: Food poisoning complaints reached 3 TWO WEEKS AGO—a 700% spike from the 0.4 weekly baseline (z-score: 5.42)—raising questions about whether a restaurant outbreak, supplier issue, or food handling problem affected Sunset Park residents.
evidence: 3 food poisoning complaints TWO WEEKS AGO vs. 0.4 weekly average (700% spike, z-score: 5.42)
Clustering suggests potential foodborne illness outbreak rather than isolated incidents
Heat/Hot Water remains top complaint (1322 over 90 days), which can exacerbate food storage/safety issues
reporting_angles: Contact NYC DOHMH to cross-reference with foodborne illness investigations and health inspections in Sunset Park
Identify whether complaints clustered around specific restaurant(s), food vendor(s), or type of cuisine

themes_detail.label: Dumpster & Hazmat Waste Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Dumpster complaints spiked 967% to 4 complaints TWO WEEKS AGO (vs. 0.4 weekly average, z-score: 5.21), and hazardous materials complaints hit 500% spike THREE WEEKS AGO (3 vs. 0.5 avg), suggesting improper waste handling across the district.
evidence: 4 dumpster complaints TWO WEEKS AGO vs. 0.4 weekly average (967% spike, z-score: 5.21)
3 hazardous materials complaints THREE WEEKS AGO vs. 0.5 weekly average (500% spike, z-score: 5.0)
Unsanitary conditions remain top 10 complaint category (250 over 90 days), indicating persistent sanitation issues
reporting_angles: Investigate whether construction/renovation activity (622 DOB permits filed) is generating improper waste disposal
Interview DSNY and environmental enforcement to identify which blocks/facilities are sources of dumpster and hazmat complaints

themes_detail.label: Abandoned Bikes Accumulating
themes_detail.summary: Abandoned bike complaints hit 4 TWO WEEKS AGO—a 540% spike from the 0.6 weekly baseline (z-score: 4.85)—suggesting rapid accumulation of debris bikes that may indicate theft, vandalism, or bike-share service gaps in the district.
evidence: 4 abandoned bike complaints TWO WEEKS AGO vs. 0.6 weekly average (540% spike, z-score: 4.85)
Community Board budget requests include 'Upgrade or provide new Select Bus Service (SBS) routes' and 'Other transit service requests,' indicating mobility concerns
Potential correlation with bike-share expansion or theft patterns in high-density residential areas
reporting_angles: Check with NYPD and Citi Bike to determine whether spike reflects bike theft, service issues, or illegal dumping
Interview residents about street clutter and whether abandoned bikes are creating pedestrian safety hazards
